title: Parameter-Free Gradient Minimization in l_p Geometry
abstract: Exact value-gradient query-complexity results for convex differentiable objectives on finite-dimensional real l_p spaces with attained minima and a positive global primal-to-dual Lipschitz-gradient bound. For finite real p > 1, the development proves strict-local scale-identification impossibility at LR/epsilon = 4 and a deterministic method family with three post-secant-initialization query-rate regimes. For p > 2 it also proves deterministic known-parameter upper and lower query exponents p/(p+2), with explicit horizon and dimension restrictions on the lower bound.

informal.V7.scaleIdentificationImpossibility: For finite real p > 1 and positive epsilon, measurable strict-local exact value-gradient methods satisfy scale-identification lower bounds on convex smooth one-dimensional objectives with unique minimizers, even at LR/epsilon = 4. The result includes deterministic and randomized finite-horizon statements and infinite worst-case expected queried-or-returned hitting time.
informal.V7.knownParameterAboveTwoOptimality: For finite real p > 2 and convex differentiable objectives with attained minima and a positive global primal-to-dual Lipschitz-gradient bound, deterministic known-parameter exact value-gradient methods have upper query exponent p/(p+2). The matching lower exponent concerns the first T queries, requires d >= 2 and 1 <= T <= d, and retains the explicit min(p, log d) dependence.
informal.V7.main: For convex differentiable objectives with attained minima and positive global L-Lipschitz gradients from l_p to its dual, one deterministic family works for every finite real p > 1 and positive epsilon after supplied nondegenerate secant initialization with 0 < M0 <= L. It returns a queried point with dual gradient norm at most epsilon. Writing R for distance to the minimizer set, the post-initialization oracle-call bound has polynomial dependence on max(1, LR/epsilon) with exponent 1/2 for 1 < p < 2 and p = 2, and p/(p+2) for p > 2, plus additive log(e + L/M0) calibration cost. Constants depend only on p, with a universal constant at p = 2; discovering the secant pair is outside the count.
